gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-inscripti: Wide, crisp, bossy letters: Azonix draws every curve like bent wire, while Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian keeps big open eyes and a deep middle band. One commands attention; the other simply lets you read.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-jp: Commanding is how Azonix looks, its curves holding the heft of a rope from start to finish. And Noto Sans JP sweeps open beneath it with a very tall x-height, giving the heading room to bark.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Azonix has zero stroke contrast, every curve bent at the same heft, which gives it a machined, wide-shouldered stance. But Noto Sans Kaithi loosens it up, its lowercase standing nearly capital-tall with an open channel in each e.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Bent-wire curves, wide and stern: that's Azonix. Noto Sans Kannada takes the edge off with gentle capitals and s curves open at both ends, so a larger heading over modest body text feels natural.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Noto Sans Kayah Li reads softly, with brush ends lifting away before each curve closes and capitals barely taller than the lowercase. And over a full page that gentle quality would carry smoothly, never tugging against the wire-bent Azonix above.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-kharoshth: Azonix is the wide, wire-bent heading here, with stroke contrast of exactly none and a stern, commanding look. But Noto Sans Kharoshthi settles into a dense, dark stripe of lowercase whose curves never close, so a long stretch of it feels warm and steady.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer brings generous openings, like a chisel notch in wood, and small letters standing nearly capital-sized. Azonix does the loud work with wire-bent s curves that never thin, while Noto Sans Khmer does the quiet work of being read.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Noto Sans Khojki lets light through its wide exits and gives every e a large, clear eye. Azonix is best at stamping out identical bar thickness across a line, and Noto Sans Khojki at staying open and easy to follow.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Azonix draws its curves without any thinning, wide and crisp even when shrunk. Noto Sans Khudawadi sits below with rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook, so a modest heading size should be plenty.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-kr: Azonix has no hairlines at all, so its stems match everything else, wide and commanding. But Noto Sans KR keeps its curve gaps generous beside a big x-height and stubby ascenders, making a long page feel open and steady.
